test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 10 May, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'** i.e.** 'Greatest'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The blank in the sentence needs an adjective that describes the extent of the reduction in stress levels.
 
• **'Greatest'** is the superlative form of the adjective 'great'. It means the highest degree or the most.
 
• In the context of this sentence,** 'greatest' **fits best because it states that the most significant reduction in perceived stress levels were reported by those who adhered to the diet most strictly.
 
• Using the correct degrees of comparison (positive, comparative, superlative) is essential in English language to distinguish between the degrees or levels of a quality.

Therefore, the **correct sentence **is: *'**Intriguingly, those who followed the psychobiotic diet reported they felt less stressed compared with those who followed the control diet. There was also a direct correlation between how strictly participants followed the diet and their perceived stress levels, with those who ate more psychobiotic foods during the four - week period reporting the **greatest **reduction in perceived stress levels.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **'Greater'** and** 'great'** are the comparative and positive forms of the term 'great' respectively. 
 
• They do not fit here because the sentence describes the highest degree of reduction, not just a high degree or a degree higher than another.
 
• **'Greatly'** is an adverb, not an adjective, and does not fit the sentence as it cannot describe a noun or pronoun. An adverb modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb.
